entry.title: Show HN: Wikipedia Importance Map. Every article sized by its pagerank on a map (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: I extracted all Wikidata items with geocoordinates, joined them with pageview statistics [1] and wikipedia pagerank scores [2] to define their label sizes. For some entities without coordinates, I used proxies: Birthplace for humans, port of registry for ships, city of the headquarters for companies. I created a version a year ago without AI. It was already interesting, but lacked a lot of polish and functionality. Now it was fun to complete it with coding agents. You can toggle the different categories on and off in the UI. People and places are off by default, because they overshadow everything else and humans overlap so much. But please turn it on if you want to see where "important" humans have been born. And the search works with a completely static index and range requests. [1]: https://github.com/athalhammer/danker [2]: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PageRank Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49094842 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

entry.title: Show HN: Get a security assessment of MCP servers directly from your terminal (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: I built a deterministic scanner that catches command injection, prompt-injection markers in tool descriptions, over-broad/destructive tools, and committed secrets in MCP servers before you connect them. It continuously scans the entire official MCP registry and makes results available at https://index.canopii.dev. Now the engine behind that scanner is available as a CLI that you can integrate into your processes and CI/CD pipelines (e.g --min-grade B). If you are building MCP servers, you can make sure your MCP server is secure using the local mode before publishing it. Or check why your server scored low, apply fixes, check if your score has improved locally first before publishing a new version so as to eliminate guesswork. If you are a user, easily check the security of an MCP server before connecting your AI agents using one of the available methods (remote, github, pypi, npm etc.) You can also use an LLM as a "judge". It won't affect the score but it may flag important security considerations that a deterministic scanner can't catch. No telemetry, no account necessary. Github: https://github.com/canopii-dev/canopii-cli (license: Apache 2.0) Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49094760 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

entry.title: Show HN: I was tired of opening 2 tabs for every HN link, so I made a userscript (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
entry.summary: HN is great for the links people share, but a big part of the value I get comes from reading the discussion around them. I realized I was always opening the article in one tab and the comments in another, constantly switching back and forth. I figured there was probably a simpler way, so I threw together this userscript to merge the two. 1. Clicking a link from Hacker News opens the article with a side panel containing the discussion. It doesn't require your credentials, is resizable, and is easy to tweak if you want to customize it. 2. If you land on an article that has previously been shared on HN, the script finds the existing discussion and adds a button in the top-right to open the panel. Feedback welcome. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49090607 Points: 298 # Comments: 76
